At Mashable, our tech reporters spend all year testing displays, PC hardware, and gaming gear. While we’ve watched component shortages and price hikes push hardware prices uncomfortably high over the last few months, Amazon is finally bringing PC gamers some relief with Prime Big Deal Days — better known as October Prime Day.

Running Oct. 6 and 7, Prime Big Deal Days is Amazon’s 48-hour event exclusively for Prime members. We’ve been covering this fall sale since its 2022 debut, using price-tracking tools like camelcamelcamel to verify that an "early deal" is a genuine price drop before we ever recommend it.

The price check is especially crucial for gaming setups, where outdated hardware can quietly bottleneck your entire system. If your GPU pumps out 144 frames per second but your monitor tops out at 60Hz, you are throwing away performance you paid for. Slow refresh rates and high response times can lead to motion blur, screen tearing, and delayed inputs in fast shooters like Valorant, Apex, or Call of Duty.

Upgrading your panel gets your display speeds back in sync with your PC. Whether you need a 280Hz eSports display for frame-rate gains, a 1440p workhorse for sharper visual detail, or a curved screen for immersive single-player games, early Prime Day deals have slashed prices across Samsung, Alienware, MSI, and more.

We rounded up the best early monitor deals live right now so you can upgrade your setup for less.

Fluid 144Hz frame rates for under $90

Finding a true 144Hz IPS display under $90 is rare, making the MSI PRO MP243L E14 an easy pick if you want fast gaming speeds on a tight budget. Jumping from a standard 60Hz or 75Hz screen to 144Hz removes distracting motion blur in fast shooters, while FreeSync support prevents screen tearing when your frame rate drops. The 24-inch 1080p panel delivers sharp pixel density with vibrant colors and wide viewing angles, making it just as solid for daily work or a cheap second display as it is for entry-level PC and console gaming.

Credit: MSI

$89.99 at Amazon
$109.99 Save $20

Score a 0.5ms tournament display for cheap

If you spend most of your gaming hours in fast-moving tactical shooters like Valorant, CS2, or Apex Legends, sheer speed matters far more than ultra-high resolutions. The MSI MAG 274CF X24 pushes a massive 240Hz refresh rate alongside an ultra-fast 0.5ms response time on a budget-friendly panel. The high frame capacity eliminates screen tearing, ghosting, and input delay, making fast target tracking feel effortless.

Credit: MSI

$129.99 at Amazon
$139.99 Save $10

Leave flat screens behind for under $190

Most curved monitors use a subtle bend, but the Samsung Odyssey G55C packs an aggressive 1000R curve that matches the natural field of view of the human eye, pulling your peripheral vision directly into single-player RPGs, flight sims, and racing games. Bumping the screen size up to 32 inches can sometimes stretch out 1080p graphics, but its sharp 1440p QHD resolution keeps textures crisp and detailed across the entire display. Pair that panoramic curve with a fast 165Hz refresh rate, FreeSync screen-tearing protection, and built-in eye saver settings to cut blue light during late-night raids, and you get pure immersion that is worth spending on.

Credit: Samsung

$189.99 at Amazon
$329.99 Save $140

Ditch 1080p blur with ASUS's 180Hz QHD monitor

Cracking the sub-$200 mark while offering both 1440p resolution and a fast 180Hz refresh rate makes the ASUS TUF Gaming VG27AQ3A an unbeatable budget upgrade. Stepping up from standard 1080p delivers 77% more screen workspace and much sharper text, while its Fast IPS panel maintains color accuracy across wide viewing angles. ASUS includes ELMB Sync (Extreme Low Motion Blur) alongside G-Sync and FreeSync support to eliminate screen tearing and ghosting in fast-moving shooters.

Credit: ASUS

$199 at Amazon
$209 Save $10

Uncap your GPU’s frame rate at 1440p

Sub-$200 gaming monitors usually top out around 165Hz or 180Hz, but the Alienware AW2726DL pushes speed even further without sacrificing resolution. Delivering a blistering 280Hz refresh rate alongside sharp 1440p visuals, this 27-inch IPS panel eliminates motion blur and input lag in fast-paced competitive shooters like Valorant and Apex Legends. Combined with 1ms response times, vibrant colors, and a fully adjustable stand that tilts, swivels, and pivots, you get top-tier eSports frame rates from a premium brand at a budget price.

Drop your display bottleneck for 39% off

Samsung’s Odyssey G5 (G50F) delivers razor-sharp 1440p resolution, 1ms response times, and a fast 180Hz refresh rate to keep high-speed motion fluid and free of input lag. The Fast IPS panel keeps colors accurate across a wide 178-degree viewing angle, while G-Sync and FreeSync support prevent screen tearing when your frame rate dips. Both the 27-inch and 32-inch options feature integrated gamer-focused tools like Black Equalizer to spot enemies in dark shadows, along with a full-motion ergonomic stand that height-adjusts, tilts, swivels, and pivots into vertical mode.

Credit: Samsung

Get an ultra-fast QD-OLED display for under $350

OLED displays used to command four-figure price tags, but MSI’s MAG 274QP QD-OLED X24 brings flagship-level panel technology down to a much more accessible price. Combining self-emitting OLED pixels with Quantum Dot color conversion, this 27-inch 1440p display delivers pure pitch-black levels, infinite contrast, and vibrant 10-bit color depth with zero backlight bleed. A blistering 240Hz refresh rate paired with an instantaneous 0.03ms response time makes fast-moving motion look blur-free.

Credit: MSI

$349.99 at Amazon
$399.99 Save $50

Unlock 360Hz speed and infinite contrast for 8% off

If you want esports-grade speed without sacrificing brilliant picture quality, the MSI MPG 271QRX QD-OLED offers the best of both worlds. A blazing 360Hz refresh rate and near-instant 0.03ms response time make fast movement look smooth and blur-free in competitive games like Valorant and Apex Legends. Plus, its QD-OLED display delivers deep blacks, rich colors, and razor-sharp 1440p detail.

Credit: MSI

$579.99 at Amazon
$629.99 Save $50

Cut 30% off a massive 180Hz curved display

If you want to ditch multi-monitor setups for a single, seamless display, Samsung’s 40-inch Odyssey G7 (G75F) brings serious screen space. Its massive 21:9 ultrawide frame runs at a razor-sharp 5120x2160 resolution, wrapping your peripheral vision with a tight 1000R curve. Despite its huge size, it doesn't sacrifice speed — delivering a smooth 180Hz refresh rate, 1ms response time, and FreeSync Premium Pro support for fluid, tear-free gameplay in fast-action games.

Credit: Samsung

At Mashable, our tech reporters spend all year testing displays, PC hardware, and gaming gear. While we’ve watched component shortages and price hikes push hardware prices uncomfortably high over the last few months, Amazon is finally bringing PC gamers some relief with Prime Big Deal Days — better known as October Prime Day.

Running Oct. 6 and 7, Prime Big Deal Days is Amazon’s 48-hour event exclusively for Prime members. We’ve been covering this fall sale since its 2022 debut, using price-tracking tools like camelcamelcamel to verify that an "early deal" is a genuine price drop before we ever recommend it.

The price check is especially crucial for gaming setups, where outdated hardware can quietly bottleneck your entire system. If your GPU pumps out 144 frames per second but your monitor tops out at 60Hz, you are throwing away performance you paid for. Slow refresh rates and high response times can lead to motion blur, screen tearing, and delayed inputs in fast shooters like Valorant, Apex, or Call of Duty.

Upgrading your panel gets your display speeds back in sync with your PC. Whether you need a 280Hz eSports display for frame-rate gains, a 1440p workhorse for sharper visual detail, or a curved screen for immersive single-player games, early Prime Day deals have slashed prices across Samsung, Alienware, MSI, and more.

We rounded up the best early monitor deals live right now so you can upgrade your setup for less.

Fluid 144Hz frame rates for under $90

Finding a true 144Hz IPS display under $90 is rare, making the MSI PRO MP243L E14 an easy pick if you want fast gaming speeds on a tight budget. Jumping from a standard 60Hz or 75Hz screen to 144Hz removes distracting motion blur in fast shooters, while FreeSync support prevents screen tearing when your frame rate drops. The 24-inch 1080p panel delivers sharp pixel density with vibrant colors and wide viewing angles, making it just as solid for daily work or a cheap second display as it is for entry-level PC and console gaming.
